The residue of $27$ modulo $4$ is the integer $0\le r<4$ such that

$$
27≡r\,(\text{mod}\,4).
$$

**Method 1**

To find the residue $r,$ we need to write $27$ as an integer multiple of $4,$ plus the residue $r.$

We note that $27≡3\,(\text{mod}\,4)$ because

$$
27=6\cdot 4+3.
$$

Therefore, the residue of $27$ modulo $4$ is $3.$

**Method 2**

We can use the subtraction property:

$$
\begin{aligned}27 & ≡27-0 &  & (\text{mod}\,4) \\  & ≡27-6\cdot 4 &  & (\text{mod}\,4) \\  & ≡27-24 &  & (\text{mod}\,4) \\  & ≡3 &  & (\text{mod}\,4)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the residue of $27$ modulo $4$ is $3.$
